when_to_use: Determine position, direction, visibility, motion trajectory or separation (including lanes/car lengths) across synchronized views. Not enumerating objects or events. Two synchronized views with referenced object identities are given; the required answer is location, direction, visibility, motion trajectory or separation, possibly measured in lanes/car lengths. Exclude enumeration of objects/events; numeric wording alone does not make a task counting.
strategy:
1. Identify the condition view/event, target view, target object and reference object; preserve the question’s frame-relative or motion-relative meaning and any distance unit. If no event time is specified, identify the requested motion interval or final state.
2. Use joint watch_videos to initialize labeled identities, track them beyond the label window and locate the event time. Inspect corresponding times in both views.
3. Observe target and reference together at that time; track the requested interval for trajectory questions. For separation, estimate in the requested unit using visible lane boundaries or a comparable vehicle length, not raw cross-view pixels. If direction, occlusion or event timing is ambiguous, re-watch a narrower synchronized range including the event transition.
4. Compare the observed relation with the options. Choose not-visible only after checking the specified view at the relevant time; do not substitute a count or infer absence from a missing report.

Constraints:
Count visible intervening lanes only when requested; vehicle-length distance is an estimate, not a vehicle count. Left/right can change with viewpoint; do not transfer image directions between cameras. Losing a label is not losing the object.
